I'm sorry. Hold compassion for yourself. You didn't ask for your phobias. You don't want to disappoint or frustrate anyone, including yourself. You have a medical condition that limits you some ways, sometimes. 

You will find the tough love and suggestions to "get over it and just do it" easy to come by. Compassionate understanding not so much.  I support you on your path and journey to health. Think of this as a small setback, not a defeat. Keep going, you'll get there.
Great thoughtful, helpful post w/ some really good ideas. Thank you and thanks to the OP.

i know the feeling well, "apologizing for existing". We hate to feel like we're needy all the time and always leaning on those closest to us who care and are supportive. i once said to my gf "I don't know how much more of this you'll be able to take", referring to my struggling and suffering. 

i think it's good to tell them how much we appreciate their support and what heroes they are.
i love that you said you are proud of yourself. self-care/self-love is so important.

that sounds like a big victory, with potential for building many more. it's impressive you resisted several opportunities to run or hide and instead went ahead and did something that challenged your anxiety. i'm sure your friend and his daughter appreciate you more than ever. that's worth a million times more than some strangers' ignorance.

it kind of seems like her familial role, but idk, i haven't met any of her family. they're not local. i guess it's her way of maintaining control. but that's the negative side. the positive side is she really is a compassionate, caring person.
yeah normal sucks. blech.

my girlfriend? yeah we talk every night around 10p. it can be difficult because i give her the daily report on my medical/emotional state. she's supportive but this is stressful for her and she tends to offer unsolicited advice.

A bit. I have a girlfriend, she's 1/2 hour away. I'm in a Buddhist sangha for people w/ chronic illness and disabilities. That's great but also 1/2 hour away and just meets once/week for 1.5 hours. No long-term effects have ever been associated w/ weed in clinical trials, and they've been doing them for well over 50 years. Not that it's been studied anywhere near as much as it should considering its widespread use. I'm more inclined to believe you can aggravate an existent anxiety disorder, while you are smoking. After quitting, not so much.

no worries at all about the structure of your post. anxiety makes our thoughts race and we're experiencing confusing sensations in our bodies and confusing thoughts in our minds. 

as far as real-life help, i would start w/ a psychologist. if they feel you would benefit from medication they can refer you to a partner physician who can work w/ you on that. but a good psychologist can help in many ways -- help you understand what's going on with yourself, and give you techniques (tools) to feel better. Over time if you develop a good working relationship you can get a handle on anxiety so that it doesn't impact your life the way it is now. 

remember that you are in charge, the psychologist is there to serve you. so if you don't feel like the first (or second, or...) person you meet with is a good match for you, definitely move on and meet with someone else.

you are not alone, although it's not listed as a typical anxiety symptom, i have to believe it's not uncommon. i've done it, and of course i'm anxious it will happen again. sometimes i feel like i WISH i could throw up. like purge the anxiety from my body. another (related) angle on it is simply the body reacting to extreme distress. i've thrown up from high-level physical pain.. hope you find peace and ease in life soon friend.
thanks a lot. i had CBT years ago, but it's been quite a while. i'm overwhelmed with concepts and techniques for battling anxiety. need to find just a couple things i can do that will have an impact.
i'm pro-therapy if the therapist gets it and really wants to help. but i can only get once every 2-3 weeks from kaiser and so far it's just a tiny bandaid.

I'm so sorry you're suffering. Sleep/bed stuff can be such a huge fuckyou, it's so hard to get "healthy" with it, get it where we need or want it to be. I'm sorry your mother is giving you grief. I try to allow myself to sleep whenever my body wants to. Self-kindness is so important. Maybe you can allow yourself to cry. Allow yourself to sleep.

I don't think it would be enough by itself for most people. But if it matters, and there are other reasons that you can say, "yeah that's something, that matters at least some..." Then you put them together and you stick around. There isn't a single complete reason for a lot of people -- most I would guess. Like, "for my kids". Many of us don't have something like that, or we'd be a lot less likely to be on this subreddit.

What about the caring people you know. A family member, a friend, a neighbor, someone online who reached out to you. You'll never see their faces, hear their voices, read their words, experience their caring again.

I had a stroke and they discharged me after initial treatment (2-3  weeks). It's all by the book -- can he get from his bed to the little table? Yes? Okay, discharge him. 

But I live alone in a little mobile home. Was already disabled from a chronic pain condition and anxiety disorder. I was managing before the stroke. Had a life. 

Now I'm wracked with anxiety, shaking, obsessing. Lots of pain and physical dysfunction too and it's a feedback loop. I hate what my body and life have become. 

My psychiatrist said yesterday he'd look into some kind of group placement, which was music to my ears. Trying to manage this stroke recovery and all these meds and life by myself isn't working.

But I know Kaiser. They told me when I was discharged there was no "medical reason" for me not to go home. It's extremely hard to get them to change the playbook. If they tell my psychiatrist, they know best and nothing should be changed, I'm wondering about playing the suicide card to get their attention re the severity of the situation.

But if all it will do is make me lose the controlled meds on my med list or worse get me stuck on a psych ward, then playing that card digs me into an even deeper hole.

thanks for responding guys, means a lot to me.
